possibly [[Karnic languages|Karnic]]) |iso3=xpa |aiatsis=L36 |glotto=pirr1240 |glottorefname=Pirriya }} '''Pirriya''' (also ''Birria'', ''Bidia'', ''Kunggari'', ''Kulumali'', and ''Kungadutji'') is an [[extinct language|extinct]] and unclassified [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]]. It was spoken by the [[Bidia people]] (also known as ''Biria'') of the western and central western Queensland, including [[Shire of Barcoo|Barcoo Shire]], Whitula Creek, [[Cooper Creek]], and [[Jundah, Queensland|Jundah]].{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/125?embed=true|title=Pirriya|publisher=[[State Library of Queensland]]|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|url-status=live|accessdate=30 May 2022}}{{SLQ-CC-BY|url=https://maps.slq.qld.gov.au/iyil/view/48?embed=true|title=Birria|publisher=[[State Library of Queensland]]|website=Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages map|url-status=live|accessdate=30 May 2022}} It is not to be confused with the [[Biri language]] and its dialects, also a [[Queensland]] language, spoken by the [[Biria people]]. == Classification == Geographically it lay between the [[Karnic language|Karnic]] and [[Maric languages|Maric]] languages, but had no obvious connection to either; the data is too poor to draw any conclusions on classification.{{cite book |author=Bowern, Claire |url=https://yale.academia.edu/ClaireBowern/Papers/1002425/Karnic_classification_revisited |title=Forty years on |publisher=Canberra Pacific Linguistics |year=2001 |editor=J Simpson |pages=245–260 |chapter=Karnic classification revisited |display-editors=etal |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211103181833/http://yale.academia.edu/ClaireBowern/Papers/1002425/Karnic_classification_revisited |url-status=live |archivedate=2021-11-03}} Dixon (2002){{cite book |last=Dixon |first=R. M. W. |url=http://www.cambridge.org/catalogue/catalogue.asp?isbn=0521473780 |title=Australian Languages: their nature and development |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2002 |author-link=R. M. W. Dixon}}{{rp|xxxiii}} classes Pirriya with [[Kungkari language|Kungkari]] as a subgroup of the Maric languages while Breen (1990) suggests it may be a Karnic language.{{cite book |last=Breen |first=Gavan |url=https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/bitstream/1885/145734/1/PL-B105.pdf |title=Salvage studies of Western Queensland Aboriginal languages |date=1990 |publisher=Pacific Linguistics |series=Pacific Linguistics B-105 |location=Canberra}}{{rp|64}} == Phonology == === Consonants === {| class="wikitable IPA" style="text-align: center;" ! ![[Front vowel|Front]] ![[Central vowel|Central]] ![[Back vowel|Back]] |- ![[Close vowel|High]] |i iː | |u (uː) |- ![[Low vowel|Low]] | |a aː | |} The long /uː/ is considered rare.{{Cite book |last1=Blake |first1=Barry J. |title=Pirriya |last2=Breen |first2=Gavan |publisher=Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, Australian National University |year=1990 |location=In Gavan Breen (ed.), Salvage studies of Western Queensland Aboriginal languages |pages=6–21}} == Vocabulary == Some words from the Birria language, as spelt and written by Birria authors include: * {{lang|xpa|Billar}}: spear * {{lang|xpa|Binoor}}: bandicoot * ''Boorong'': rock * ''Bowra'': kangaroo * ''Burlo moori'': good day * ''Gulburri'': emu * ''Noka'': water * ''Ullatah'': moon ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == * [http://aiatsis.gov.au/sites/default/files/docs/collections/language_bibs/birria_biria_pirriya.pdf Bibliography of Pirriya people and language resources], at the [[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]] {{Authority control}} [[Category:Unclassified languages of Australia]] [[Category:Karnic languages]] [[Category:Extinct languages of Queensland]] {{ia-lang-stub}}
